newsitem.title: USA: United Healthcare earnings fall, hit HMO group.
newsitem.headline: United Healthcare earnings fall, hit HMO group.

text.p: United Healthcare Corp. said Thursday its profits soared 33 percent in the second quarter, but the nation's leading health maintenance company said certain of its businesses fared poorly and threatened to erode full-year results.

That admission drove the company's stock down sharply and sparked an broad sell-off on companies that run health maintenance organisations. United Healthcare slumped $4.94 to close at $53.125 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the fifth most active issue.
United Healthcare said earnings for the quarter rose to $116 million from $87 million in the same year-ago period.
Earnings per share rose to 57 cents, in line with Wall Street estimates and up from 43 cents a share, excluding special items, a year earlier.

But the Minneapolis-based HMO said profit margins lagged in Maryland, Rhode Island and the Gulf Coast, reducing net income in the second quarter by about 6 cents a share and posing a threat to earnings for the remainder of the year.

"We are of course pleased with the progress made during the second quarter," said Chairman William McGuire. "However, we are now focusing significant resources to ensure improved performance in a few health plan markets...in which we have not yet reached margins achieved in aggregate by our other health plans."
"While improved performance is expected in these markets, the performance at these health plans will continue to be a drag on earnings for the remainder of 1997," he added.
The company said revenues for the second quarter rose 18 percent, to $2.9 billion.
Signs of declining HMO enrollment, coupled with concern over rising medical costs, have weighed heavily on health care stocks this week, analysts said.
On Tuesday, Aetna Inc., one of the country's biggest health insurers, saw its stock tumble more than 10 percent after it reported slower-than-expected growth in its HMO and Medicare plans.

Aetna's shares continued to slide Thursday after United HealthCare released its earnings, falling $4.375 to close Thursday at $97.625 on the NYSE. Aetna's stock has slumped nearly 17 percent from Monday's closing price of $117.
Oxford Health Plans Inc. also got caught in the downdraft, even after posting slightly higher-than-expected second-quarter earnings earlier this week. Oxford slumped $5.25 to $74 on Nasdaq.
"We've had two or three down days in the (HMO) group, and it all started with Aetna guiding earnings estimates lower," said Gary Frazier, a Bear, Stearns managing director.

"United and Aetna are bellwethers, so people are concerned their problems could be affecting the industry," Frazier said, adding he would probably trim his 1997 earnings estimate for United Healthcare to about $2.25 per share from $2.40.
